r.문화권·종교: Mostly Catholic · Hungarian, a rare Uralic language in Europe
r.경제 체제: Market economy · car and battery plants, eager to attract foreign investment
r.주식시장 시가총액: $62.6 billion, 25% of GDP (2025, listed domestic companies)
r.한국이 파는 것: Inorganic chemicals 31%, Vaccines, blood products 23%, Electronics, electrical equipment 11%, Machinery, computers 8% (2025, share of value)
r.한국이 사는 것: Electronics, electrical equipment 32%, Computers 14%, Other machinery, computers 9%, Cars 8% (2025, share of value)
r.한국과 맺은 FTA: Korea-EU FTA (provisionally applied 2011, fully in force 2015)
r.정치 구도: A parliamentary system led by the prime minister. From 2010, Prime Minister Orban's Fidesz ruled for years and clashed with the EU over its grip on the media and courts. The opposition Tisza won the April 2026 election, bringing a change of government.

t.why: On the Danube, it is a crossroads between Eastern and Western Europe. Having lived through the 1956 uprising against the Soviets and the 1989 transition, how to handle communist-era records is still a political issue.
t.rel: Long friendly toward Russia, it clashed often with the EU. Repairing relations is the task after the 2026 change of government, and Hungarian minorities in neighboring countries are a constant diplomatic issue.
t.korea: Korean battery makers such as Samsung SDI and SK On have built big plants there, making it one of the top destinations for Korean investment in Europe. Environmental and water-use issues around the plants sometimes make local news.
t.know: Budapest was formed in 1873 by merging Buda, Pest and Obuda on both banks of the Danube.
t.etext: German, Korean and Chinese car and battery plants are clustered there. Manufacturing is strong, but EU funds frozen over disputes with Brussels have been a burden.
